A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRACER framework and POLITIFACT-HIDDEN benchmark. Text, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable, including the new Appendix C in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original evidence-alignment and intent-generation experiments, fact-verification comparisons, a qualitative example, and component ablations in Section 6 and Tables 5–9.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds per-class results, LLaMA2-7B evaluation, and claim-length analysis in Section 6.4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The evidence alignment, intent generation, assumption inference, counterfactual filtering, evidence retrieval, and final reassessment procedures remain the same. Revised diagrams and explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14,994 political claims and the same half-truth verification task. The LLaMA2-7B experiment and length-based partitions reuse existing test coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain QACheck, ProgramFC, CHECKWHY, Flan-T5, CoT, and HiSS, alongside the unchanged alignment and intent-generation comparators. LLaMA2-7B is an additional HiSS backbone configuration.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation with LLaMA2-7B, per-class F1 reporting, and four word-count groups containing 755, 893, 308, and 44 test claims. Existing dataset splits and stated training budgets are unchanged; newly disclosed backbone and annotation-review details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the diagnostic questions examined: Table 9 checks whether Half-True gains sacrifice other classes, Table 11 examines backbone portability, and Table 12 examines performance across claim lengths. The original component ablation and utility-bill case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised annotation-agreement counts and percentages provide descriptive results rather than new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive per-class, backbone, and claim-length results, including LLaMA2-7B with reassessment at 82.3 accuracy and 65.4 macro-F1. Table 4 replaces agreement values of 96.0/96.0/91.0/86.0% with 98.9/98.9/98.8/92.1% and positive-confirmation counts; v1's unspecified denominators prevent interpreting this as a comparable improvement. Table 7 corrects CoT and HiSS test macro-F1 gains from 3.8/6.4 to 3.7/6.3, while retaining the underlying scores.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions and counterfactual reasoning remain equivalent. The removed subproblem summary repeats material retained elsewhere, and neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same task formulation, omission-and-intent benchmark, modular TRACER framework, and approximately 16-point Half-True F1 improvement. The new experiments support retained claims rather than redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds the interpretation that the main models' Half-True improvements do not sacrifice other classes, and suggests that longer claims help through richer context for intent and assumptions. The political-domain and ambiguous-intent limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised future release with a repository address for code and data. It also identifies GPT-4o-mini as the default baseline backbone, GPT-3.5-turbo for HiSS, and two independent annotators reviewing 100 intent samples. These are newly documented details; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chong et al. (2025), Tang et al. (2021), and Tang et al. (2025), including a distinction between comprehensive event retrieval and downstream fact verification. Removed duplicate references represent retained works, not substantive removals.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording and terminology edits, trims repeated task and intent explanations, updates the affiliation, and adds acknowledgments and Appendix C. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The overview is substantially redrawn and moved from v1 Figure 2 to v2 Figure 1. Appendix prompt figures become titled boxes, with four evaluation prompts consolidated into one color-coded display. Table 4 gains count columns, and new Tables 9, 11, and 12 expand the results presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through per-class diagnostics, clearer backbone and annotation-review disclosures, repository access information, and more readable diagrams and prompts. These gains are limited by ambiguous backbone matching in Appendix C: Section 6.4 gives the LLaMA2 baseline as 78.2 accuracy and 59.1 macro-F1, while Table 11 lists an unspecified HiSS baseline at 78.3 and 59.4. The original method and main experimental evidence remain stable.
